concerns.text: FR-001 mandates acquiring at least one public dataset with experimental permeability coefficients, yet the project’s own research notes state that no verified open dataset contains such measurements. Without a reachable target column the requirement cannot be satisfied, making the functional requirement untestable.

FR-004 requires the stratified split to preserve class distributions within an absolute [deferred] point difference, but the concrete tolerance is left as a placeholder. Without a numeric threshold there is no deterministic way to verify compliance, rendering the requirement untestable.

The specification assumes the existence of at least one public dataset containing experimental permeability coefficients (FR-001), yet the original idea explicitly states that no verified open dataset provides such target values. This makes the core research question—whether a GNN outperforms a descriptor‑based RF on experimental permeability—unanswerable as written.

Because the required target data are unavailable, the spec lacks any mitigation strategy (e.g., acquisition of proprietary data, creation of a surrogate target, or redesign of the research question). This omission leaves a critical gap in the functional scope.

FR-013 (descriptor ablation study) is not mentioned in the original idea. Introducing a full ablation experiment expands the scope beyond the stated goal of comparing GNN vs baseline RF and adds substantial implementation and analysis work not requested.

FR-014 (descriptor‑curation bias check) also was not part of the initial idea. While bias checks can be good practice, this requirement was not justified by the original research question and therefore represents scope creep.

SC-003 defines a Spearman rank‑correlation between SHAP descriptor rankings (RF) and GNNExplainer substructure rankings (GNN). The idea never proposed such a cross‑space correlation, and the metric is scientifically dubious because the two rankings are derived from fundamentally different feature spaces. This redefines the interpretability assessment in a way not aligned with the original question.

FR-001 requires acquiring at least one public dataset containing experimental permeability coefficients, yet the accompanying research notes state that no verified open datasets contain such measurements. Without a target variable, the core research question (whether a GNN outperforms a descriptor‑based RF on permeability) cannot be answered, rendering the downstream functional requirements and success criteria untestable.

SC-003 proposes measuring interpretability agreement via Spearman rank‑correlation between the SHAP descriptor ranking (global molecular descriptors) and the GNNExplainer substructure ranking (local graph motifs). These rankings inhabit fundamentally different feature spaces, so the correlation lacks a clear scientific interpretation and may produce misleading conclusions.

responses.response: Revised FR-001 to allow use of a high‑quality surrogate permeability dataset when experimental data are unavailable, providing a concrete mitigation strategy.
responses.what_changed: FR-001 text expanded to include surrogate dataset option and justification.

responses.response: Replaced the placeholder in FR-004 with a concrete tolerance of ≤ 5 percentage‑point difference for class distribution preservation.
responses.what_changed: FR-004 placeholder [deferred] replaced with "≤ 5 percentage‑point difference".

responses.response: Same mitigation as testability-949598b0; FR-001 now explicitly permits surrogate data, making the scope realistic.
Added a clear fallback strategy in FR-001 for cases where no experimental dataset exists, satisfying the missing mitigation requirement.
Removed FR-013 (descriptor ablation study) as it was not part of the original idea and constituted scope creep.
Removed FR-014 (bias check) because it was out‑of‑scope and created a broken reference.
responses.what_changed: Deleted FR-014 line from Requirements and removed its reference from Assumptions.

responses.response: Rewrote SC-003 to drop the scientifically dubious Spearman correlation and retain only the overlap‑based interpretability metric.
responses.what_changed: SC-003 text modified to require at least 3 of the top‑5 features overlap; Spearman clause removed.

responses.response: Addressed by the same FR-001 revision providing a surrogate‑dataset fallback, restoring scientific viability.
Resolved by revising SC-003 to use a valid overlap metric instead of an inappropriate cross‑space correlation.

new_concerns.text: SC-003 defines interpretability agreement as requiring at least 3 of the top‑5 features to be common between the GNNExplainer substructure ranking and the SHAP descriptor ranking. Since these rankings are derived from fundamentally different feature spaces (local graph substructures vs global molecular descriptors), the notion of “common” features is ill-defined, making the metric non‑meaningful and scientifically unsound.

Prior concern scientific_soundness-0b7c5687 remains unresolved because the surrogate‑dataset fallback introduced in FR-001 does not guarantee that the target permeability values are independent of the molecular descriptors; many simulation‑derived permeability estimates are themselves functions of the same descriptors, risking circular validation.
